1.explanation:
1. We forward the Android device’s DevTools socket to localhost:9222 (`adb forward tcp:9222 localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote`).
2. We invoke the Lighthouse CLI exactly as in the bug report: disabling screen emulation, disabling UA spoofing, using DevTools CPU throttling at 1× (to match the real device), and pointing at port 9222.
3. Upon opening the resulting HTML report, the footer still displays “Emulated Moto G4…” and the Moto G4 device icon, reproducing the bug.  

The Node script alternative shows how you’d do the same run programmatically.  Both approaches produce the same faulty report footer labeling the run as emulated despite running on a physical device.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse CLI against a real Android device (a Moto Power G) with screen emulation disabled, no UA spoofing, and DevTools‐based throttling, the HTML report footer still labels the run as “Emulated Moto G4 with Lighthouse 9.6.8” and shows the Moto G4 device icon, rather than indicating that it was run on a physical device.
